title: Sales Order Agent - Working with a Personal or Shared Folder (2026)

chapters.title: Setting up a test folder and email account
Managing pending tasks and testing with emails
Switching back to shared mailbox and folder support

features.name: Sales Order Agent folder selection
features.description: The sales order agent can be configured to monitor a specific folder in Outlook instead of the inbox, allowing selective email processing for testing or shared mailbox scenarios.
caveats: Do not point the agent to your inbox
Requires initial folder creation in Outlook

features.name: Sales Order Agent email conversion
features.description: The sales order agent can automatically pick up emails from a monitored folder and convert them into quotes.

features.name: Stop pending tasks in Sales Order Agent
features.description: Users can stop all pending tasks with a single click in the sales order agent interface.

features.name: Sales Order Agent shared mailbox support
features.description: Folder selection for the sales order agent is supported for shared mailboxes as well as personal accounts, maintaining control over which emails are processed.

quotes.text: Did you know there's an easy way to try the sales order agent on your own without complicated setup?
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes that the sales order agent can be tested easily, setting the context for the tutorial

quotes.text: Do not point the agent to your inbox. You only want your selected emails to be processed, not all of them
quotes.why_it_matters: Critical configuration instruction that prevents unintended email processing

quotes.text: If you already have many pending tasks, which you don't need, you can stop them all with a single click
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes a capability to bulk-clear pending tasks in the agent

quotes.text: Folder selection is supported for shared mailboxes as well. So you remain in control of which emails are processed by the agent
quotes.why_it_matters: Confirms that folder selection works for shared mailboxes, expanding the use cases beyond personal testing
